symptom: Access-rule constraints comparing a token with a member of the wrong type — a date token on a String or Integer, '[%DayLength%]' on an Integer, '[%UserRole_X%]' on a String or DateTime, '[%CurrentUser%]' on an association to a non-user entity — passed check and exec; mx check 11.14.0 reported CE0161.
cause: literalTypeProblem judged only [%CurrentUser%] and returned silence for every other token; walkXPathLiteralComparisons saw only bare identifiers, so a qualified association operand (a QualifiedNameExpr) was never compared at all.
fix: xpathTokenTypeProblem judges the measured date/length/role token pairings (others stay silent); xpathMemberName lets the walk see qualified association operands, and currentUserAssociationProblem refuses '[%CurrentUser%]' on an association whose destination is not System.User or a specialization of it.
insight: An earlier test listed '[Cnt = '[%DayLength%]']' among the legal twins with a comment saying it was measured CE0161 but not modelled — 'not judged' had been encoded as 'legal'. When a control list carries such a case, it is a TODO, not a measurement; move it when the rule lands.
test: mdl/executor/validate_access_rule_tokens_2189_test.go TestAccessRuleXPath_TokenTypes (the issue's 7 refused and 4 legal cases)
